finding: Cost model assumed every alerted fraud is stopped; only auto-hold acts before authorisation
resolution: Operational simulation (notebook 06) is the headline: saving $189,544 vs rules under the same policy (95% CI $149,958-$231,379); notebook-03 figure kept as an idealised upper bound

finding: New fraud patterns are invisible to PSI; a 50-a-month below-threshold sample finds almost nothing
resolution: Review the whole monitor-only band with spare capacity (~6.3 near-miss frauds/month); add score-tail PSI; fast labels from customer reports and dispositions

finding: Error-rate gaps by age and gender, with no tolerance defined
resolution: Card-bootstrap intervals and proposed tolerances in notebook 06; worst age band 65+: 1.66x the lowest false-alert rate (CI 1.32-2.25). Compliance sign-off and a proxy analysis are needed before go-live

finding: SMOTE creates impossible synthetic records (fractional categories and hours) and was compared under a different encoding
resolution: Recommended: switch to class weights or no weighting (validation PR-AUC within 0.005, notebook 02) and re-validate before production

finding: Validation set reused for early stopping, tuning, imbalance choice and all thresholds
resolution: Test set untouched until the end; validation results are optimistic. Use rolling time-series CV plus a separate threshold window in production

finding: City population works as a customer identifier; most test cards also appear in train
resolution: Drop or coarsen the feature and validate on unseen cards before production

finding: Card history length grows with calendar time (tenure / time proxy)
resolution: Documented in the model-risk file; cap or drop before production

finding: Standard PSI cannot see changes among alerting scores; December 'no retrain' used immature labels
resolution: Score-tail PSI and trigger added (notebook 05); December conclusion marked provisional

finding: Benchmark rules were built for this project; annualised saving extrapolated from synthetic data
resolution: Rules described as a proxy for the current process; saving reported for the test period with a confidence interval; the annualised figure is removed

finding: Capacity check ignored L2, supervisor and customer-contact work, and peak days
resolution: p95-day staffing by role in notebook 06: about 2.4 staff-hours/day across roles

finding: Auto-hold requires immediate customer contact, but most holds are overnight
resolution: 90% of holds are at 22:00-04:00; workflow now specifies automated 24/7 confirmation with a time-out rule

finding: Headline precision is not what analysts see in the review queues
resolution: Review-queue precision reported separately (4% in the simulation)

finding: No friction cost for wrongly held customers; auto-hold was charged as an analyst review
resolution: Simulation charges $1 per hold + $10 per wrongly held customer (61 on test)

finding: The recall-target option missed its 80% target on test
resolution: Thresholds need a safety margin and must be recalibrated on matured recent data

finding: Case report recommended a hold for a priority-review alert
resolution: Recommended action now follows the band's workflow (route to L1 priority review; contact before disposition)

finding: Case selection described inaccurately; the card's earlier confirmed fraud was not reported; no contrary evidence
resolution: Selection rule stated; confirmed fraud older than 60 days reported; 'facts that do not fit' section added

finding: Time windows unlabelled; dispositions and roles did not match the workflow; hindsight label in the same file
resolution: Windows labelled; dispositions and roles aligned; hindsight outcome moved to a separate file
